note: P4280 (Pro 26:15) — the sluggard buries his hand in the dish; it wears him out to lift it to his mouth.

dims.v: sloth — too lazy even to feed himself
the sluggard so sunk in laziness that, having put his hand in the dish, he is too weary to bring it back to his mouth — sloth at its absurd extreme
the weariness it feels at the least effort (266213)
welded to the exhaustion the smallest task costs him

atsel (sluggard) — 'the SLUGGARD buries his hand in the dish; it wears him out to bring it back to his mouth' (cf 19:24); sloth grown so total it will not lift food to feed itself. Emergent: laziness as a self-defeating paralysis, comic and tragic at once.
enervation — the sluggard exhausted by the least effort
the weariness that overcomes the sluggard at the least exertion — the enervation that makes even self-feeding too much trouble
welded to the laziness that produces it
laah (be weary/exhausted) — 'it WEARS him out to bring it back to his mouth'; the sluggard is exhausted by the smallest task. Sloth turns the least effort into an unbearable labour.
